key_claims: Caffeine has a half-life of 5-7 hours, meaning 500mg of caffeine is reduced to 250mg after 5-7 hours and 125mg after 10-14 hours
A double espresso at 4 p.m. leaves approximately 250mg of caffeine in your system at 11 p.m. when trying to sleep
Eight hours in bed does not equal eight hours of sleep; accounting for 45 minutes to fall asleep and two 15-minute interruptions reduces actual sleep to under 7 hours
Open loops (unresolved questions or conversations) before bed impair sleep quality and should be avoided
The solution to constant fatigue is the intersection of three variables: sleep, diet, and training — not supplements or external products
specific_numbers: 500mg caffeine reduced to 250mg after 5-7 hours, 125mg after 10-14 hours
7 hours actual sleep (accounting for 45 minutes to fall asleep and two 15-minute interruptions)
